newsitem.title: USA: Stock market surges to record high on jobs data.
newsitem.headline: Stock market surges to record high on jobs data.

text.p: Stocks soared to record highs Thursday after the June employment report confirmed the economy is slowing at a pace that would keep the Federal Reserve from raising interest rates.
The Dow Jones industrial average ended up 100.43 points, or 1.29 percent, at 7,895.81, eclipsing its June 20 record close of 7,796.51. For the week, the blue-chip index was up 208.09 points.
In the broader market, advancing issues swamped declines 1,976 to 752 on volume of 374 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The broad rally also lifted secondary indexes to record levels.
The market closed early at 1 p.m. EDT/1700 GMT prior to Friday's Independence Day holiday.
Wall Street was in a bullish mood after fresh employment and wage data offered further evidence that the economy's growth remains moderate and inflation remains at bay.
The Labour Department said the jobless rate rose to 5.0 percent in June from a 24-year low of 4.8 percent in May.
In addition, monthly job growth and hourly wage increases were slightly lower than forecast.
Analysts said the data, which came one day after the Fed voted to hold interest rates steady, diminished chances for future increases.
"The economic backdrop at this point appears to be remarkable," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co.
"Inflation is nowhere to be found and investors are beginning to sense the August Fed meeting may also be one where rates are held in check," he said.
Analysts also detected a seasonal note in the market's performance, pointing out that the Independence Day holiday has produced more than its share of market fireworks in the past.
"Historically, the stock market usually makes a strong move, in either direction, in the days preceding the Fourth of July," said Gail Dudack, chief investment strategist at UBS Securities.
Such was the case a year ago, when a stunningly strong jobs report on the day after the Independence Day holiday initiated a stiff, summer-long stock market correction.
Any fears of a repeat performance dissipated after Thursday morning's report, which produced a fierce round of buying that remained intact through the market's close.

Among individual issues, Northrop Grumman Corp. surged 21 points to 109-7/8 after the company announced it would merge with defence aerospace giant Lockheed Martin Corp. in a stock swap deal valued at $11.6 billion. Lockheed fell 4-7/8 to 99-1/8.

Pharmaceutical company Pharmacia & Upjohn Inc. rose 1-5/8 to 37-5/16 despite announcing that its second quarter earnings would fail to exceed first-quarter levels. Instead, investors focused on the company's restructuring that it said would turn its operations around in 1998.
INSO Corp. slid 9-11/16 to 11-1/16. Alex. Brown downgraded the shares following INSO's announcement late Wednesday that second-quarter results would fall short of expectations.
The Nasdaq Composite index gained 12.00 points to 1,467.61, a new high.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 12.89 to 916.92, a new high. The American Stock Exchange index rose 4.28 to 634.34.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 5.97 to 477.68, a new high. The average share was up 56 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was at a new high of 8,639.340, up 97.831, or 1.15 percent.
